archetypes.name: anchor-verifier
archetypes.rationale: Catches plans whose step actions target specific line numbers or function-boundary ranges that have drifted since the plan was written, producing edits in wrong locations or missed insertion points.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every line number, line range, or function-boundary range cited in the plan (e.g. 'lines 21-23', 'lines 500-581', 'lines 1746/1797/1836/1878'), read the target file and verify the cited content actually appears at those lines today. Flag any anchor that is off by more than a few lines or that names the wrong content. For insertion plans ('add X beside Y at line N'), confirm that Y is present at line N and that inserting X there would not duplicate an already-existing definition. For awk range extractors like /^_run_post_apply_pipeline\(\)/,/^}$/, confirm the extracted body still ends at a simple closing brace at column zero and that no nested closing brace would truncate the extraction prematurely. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-contract
archetypes.rationale: Catches plans that add or move code exercised by eval-isolated test harnesses without updating every export list and match expression those harnesses rely on, leaving tests that silently test stub behavior instead of the new code.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each eval-isolated bash -c block in the test harness that extracts a function via awk and calls it, verify that every variable the extracted function reads (directly or via sourced helpers) is listed in the inner export statement of that bash -c call. When the plan moves code from an inline heredoc to an external file, check that the new file path variable is exported in every such inner bash -c block, not only at the outer scope. For PYWRAP basename-match patterns, confirm the glob or suffix used to intercept the new helper (e.g. ending with dedup-plan-lines.py) cannot also match sibling Python files invoked in the same code path (e.g. .plan-review-loop-dedup.py), and that the new integration test exercises the LOOP_REASON=dedup-python-failed caller-wiring path end-to-end rather than only unit-testing the helper in isolation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
